tone_statements.citation: Lugbarati Language Board [drafted by Constance Kutsch Lojenga, SIL LEAD facilitator, per PDF document properties; NCDC / USAID-RTI School Health and Reading Program]. 2013. Lugbarati [Lʉgbara Ti] Orthography Guide, revised version, December 2013. Arua: Lugbarati Language Board. 33 pp. (distributed at lugbarati.org as 'Lugbara Orthography 2014 -- Orthography-Approved').
tone_statements.quote: p. 3: 'Lugbarati is tonal with three level tones: Low, Mid, and High and a Rising contour tone while some syllables have a HM contour tone. Tone has a very heavy functional load, both in the lexicon and in the grammar. It needs to be represented in the orthography.' -- p. 11, sec. 4 'Tone': '[Lugbara]ti has three level tones, Low, Mid, High, and, much rarer, a rising contour tone, LH or a falling contour tone HL. It is not yet completely clear what is causing these. This needs further research. There are also syllables with a HM contour. These sound a lot longer and are probably two vowels, the first with a H tone, the second with a M tone.'
tone_statements.locator: Introduction p. 3 and sec. 4 'Tone' p. 11 (subsections 4.1-4.2 pp. 11-14); the language name at the start of sec. 4 is set in an embedded Doulos SIL font whose glyphs do not, hence '[Lugbara]ti'

tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (L, M, H) + contours LH, HL (rare) and HM (probably bimoraic H+M)

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Nothing. The phonology and 'Intonation' chapters (read in full from the Rosetta Project scan of pp. 1-13) describe tone only: three marked tone levels (high/mid/low) plus combined tones, 'actually five distinct tone levels' (§53, p. 11), tone rules for verbs and inter-tonic reaction. Dialect basis: 'the dialect spoken around Arua.. i.e. the dialect of the Aivu and Padzulu' (p. viii). The contents entries 'Stressing of Verbs §§426-30 p. 96' and 'The stressing ni §§561-71 p. 142' concern emphasis, not prosodic stress.

sources.note: First-hand orthography statement (SIL LEAD-facilitated 2013 workshop analysis): Lugbarati is tonal with three level tones Low, Mid, High, plus much rarer rising LH and falling HL contours and syllables with an HM contour (analysed as probably two vowels H+M, sounding longer); tone has a very heavy functional load in lexicon and grammar; orthography marks L with grave, H with acute, M unmarked, LH/HL with combined accents. Sec. 4.1 gives lexical minimal sets (e.g. ewa L.H 'elephant' vs H.H 'beer'; ori 'fear/snake/louse'; ti 'cow/mouth'); sec. 4.2 lists grammatical tone: singular vs plural noun…
